head: 1f725cedc5c8b092c8a3d7e408793ef72840ec7e
notes: Chunk 'server' covers internal/server/*.go, its templates and assets.css, no partners. Scope follows ACTION-REVIEW-SEC-001: skill/hook/settings files are not part of this chunk (none live under internal/server), so nothing was excluded on that basis. Diff is large (48 files, ~2500 inserted lines) but almost entirely additive feature work (profile/presentation audience split, bootstrap wrapper, i18n catalog, config-sync UI, worktree-status page) plus one explicit security addition: sameOriginGuard (server.go) is a new CSRF defense (Fetch-Metadata + Origin fallback) wrapping every mutating route in Handler(); reviewed it in full, found it sound (cross-site/same-site Sec-Fetch-Site rejected outright, Origin-host fallback when that header is absent, and only truly header-less — i.e. non-browser — callers pass through). No secrets are rendered or logged anywhere in the diff: handleRoutineTokenAdd documents 'write-only, never rendered or logged' and the templates/server.go funcs never surface TokenPath/TokenName values; verified by grepping the templates for any Token* field. All HTML output goes through html/template with auto-escaping; the only template.HTML-returning helpers used by this chunk (nameWrap, pathWrap in server.go) escape per rune/segment before concatenating, so no XSS was found. Cross-chunk notes: the smine-nightly bootstrap pipeline this chunk kicks off (cmd/bootstrap/run.sh) and the skills.go file-serving handlers referenced by skills_analytics_test.go are out of this chunk — if another lane reviews cmd/bootstrap or internal/server/skills.go, worth cross-checking whether the child bootstrap process ever echoes the OAUTH token or other secrets to stdout/stderr, since that output lands in the world-readable log this lane flagged (security-MIN-1) under LOG-005.

findings.claim: handleWelcomeBootstrap writes the multi-hour bootstrap run's combined stdout/stderr to a fixed, predictable path in the shared OS temp directory (os.TempDir()+"smine-bootstrap.log") opened with mode 0o644 (world-readable). The bootstrap run is a real headless claude session with tool access over the user's repos, so its log can contain prompts (including the attacker-/user-supplied extra-prompt field), file contents the agent reads back, and any verbose/error output the child process or the claude CLI itself emits. On a machine with other local accounts, any other user can read this log (mode 644, predictable name, shared temp dir), and a second concurrent/overlapping bootstrap run (or any other local process) can also overwrite/append to it since the path never varies and the file is opened O_APPEND|O_CREATE without O_EXCL.
findings.fix: Create the log under a per-run, non-predictable path with 0o600 permissions — e.g. os.CreateTemp(os.TempDir(), "smine-bootstrap-*.log") (which also yields a unique name) and os.Chmod(f.Name(), 0o600), or write it under the server's own private state dir instead of the shared OS temp dir.
findings.evidence: Re-read internal/server/bootstrap.go lines 36-111 (handleWelcomeBootstrap) in full at the pinned head: logPath is built once from os.TempDir() with a constant basename and opened with os.OpenFile(logPath, os.O_CREATE|os.O_APPEND|os.O_WRONLY, 0o644) — no per-run uniqueness and a world-readable mode. cmd.Stdout/cmd.Stderr both point at this file, and the spawned process is the real multi-hour bootstrap pipeline (cmd/bootstrap/run.sh) described in the function's own comment as resolving claude through the login shell and running the full mining/apply pipeline — i.e. its output is not trivial boilerplate but live agent activity. Confirmed grep shows exactly one os.TempDir() site in the diff (internal/server/bootstrap.go:71) and the mode literal 0o644 at line 72, both unchanged from how I first read them. Exposure is rated 'rare' rather than 'often' because the default deployment target (FACT-REPO-ARCH context: a personal macOS automation tool, routines run via launchd under the same user) is single-user, so the cross-account read primarily matters on a shared/multi-user machine — a real but non-default configuration, and I could not reach this chunk's claude-cli/run.sh to confirm whether the logged output would ever include the OAUTH token itself (that script is outside this chunk's scope, noted above).
